Would leave no stars if possible. Have made a claim to my insurance company that I have a historical condition which is still active. They have no evidence to back this up, no longer take medication, and have been discharged from services for 15 years. Not sure if they are reading my correspondence, for example last communication was about what evidence they had for the present day but referred me to information that was written in 2006 15 years ago. They seem to think people cannot get better.  Would not recommend for patients who require Life insurance or occupational health where medical record accuracy is seriously important. The matter is with the ICO although I am leaving the surgery as I have lost trust. Simply no rational explanation for commenting on my present day health the way that they have done.

Receptionists could be more helpful but not too bad. I am considering legal action but even I won it would be more of a academic victory as I have now been to a specialist insurer, I just don't have insurance for the area that I previously suffered with and will not do so until a doctor declares I have not had any issues for 5 years which is now true but Queens Avenue have wrongly described my condition as active and chronic when it was acute and lasted for one week. Related issues for 4 years but still nothing in this area of medicine since 2011. No paperwork exists beyond 2011 so why Queens Avenue feel they can describe as not only active but chronic make my mind boggle.

I have informed my parents that their health and Welfare POA will have to be dealt with by others as I am not prepared to work with Drs who make statements without evidence and refuse when asking to outline the evidence to back up their assertions. The surgery has a duty to represent my present day circumstances with present day evidence.
Paul Eyres
